keurig k slim single serve pod coffee ma.product_name: Keurig K-Slim single-serve K-Cup pod coffee maker (K-Slim, model K900 / K-Slim family)

moving_parts.how: Grip the moulded handle on the top front of the brew head and lift up and back; the handle is rigidly joined to the K-Cup pod assembly housing lid, so raising it swings the whole brew head lid open rearward and exposes the K-Cup pod holder and funnel opening. A pod drops in; lowering the handle closes the lid, drives the entrance needle down through the pod foil and latches the head shut ready to brew. Lifting and lowering it also wakes/powers the brewer on.
moving_parts.axis: across its width (left-right horizontal pin at the back of the brew head), lid swings in the front-to-back vertical plane
moving_parts.pivot: horizontal hinge pin at the rear top edge of the K-Cup pod assembly housing, behind the pod holder

moving_parts.how: A loose (non-hinged) cap sitting on top of the 46 oz reservoir at the rear/left of the brewer; lift it straight up off the reservoir mouth to expose the fill opening, then set it back down flat. The manual's first step is 'Remove the water reservoir lid, then lift the reservoir straight up to remove it… Replace lid.'
moving_parts.axis: vertical (straight up off the tank mouth)
moving_parts.pivot: no pin — lifts off the rim of the reservoir opening

moving_parts.how: With the lid off, lift the tank straight up out of its cradle on the side/rear of the brewer body to carry it to the sink for filling to the MAX FILL line; to refit, lower it straight down until the lock tabs on the tank engage the brewer. Removing it exposes the reservoir well and the water outlet port in the brewer base.
moving_parts.axis: vertical (straight up, parallel to the brewer's height)
moving_parts.pivot: comes off its seat in the reservoir well; located by lock tabs that engage the brewer body

moving_parts.part: Drip tray assembly (drip tray plate + drip tray + drip tray base)
moving_parts.how: Grasp the tray at the front and slide it horizontally toward you out of the guide slot under the brew spout, keeping it level so the up-to-8 oz of collected overflow does not spill; it comes free at the end of the track. Removing it reveals the recessed base and the tall mug platform, giving clearance for travel mugs up to about 7 in tall.
moving_parts.axis: front to back (pulled forward along the brewer's depth axis)
moving_parts.pivot: no pin — runs on the horizontal rails/slot in the brewer base, pulls off the front

moving_parts.part: Drip tray plate (grid the mug stands on)
moving_parts.how: Once the tray is out, the perforated plate lifts straight up off the top of the drip tray reservoir for emptying and washing, exposing the catch basin below.
moving_parts.axis: vertical (lifts off the top face of the tray)
moving_parts.pivot: no pin — rests in the lip of the drip tray

moving_parts.how: Cleaning only: unplug the brewer, remove the drip tray, lift the handle fully, then push up from underneath the holder with a finger through the opening in the base of the pod housing and lift the holder out of the top. Mind the exit needle underneath. It refits by pressing straight down into the housing until it clicks.
moving_parts.axis: vertical (pushed up and out of the brew head)
moving_parts.pivot: no pin — snaps out of the K-Cup pod assembly housing

moving_parts.part: Funnel (part of the pod holder assembly)
moving_parts.how: Cleaning only: with the pod holder removed, grip the holder and twist/pull the funnel apart from the top of the holder; it snaps back on by pushing it straight back over the holder rim. Separating them exposes the exit needle in the holder base for rinsing.
moving_parts.axis: along the part (pulled off along the holder's vertical axis, with a slight twist about that axis)
moving_parts.pivot: no pin — friction/snap fit on the top of the K-Cup pod holder

moving_parts.how: Momentary illuminated button on the front control panel; press in horizontally (toward the back of the brewer) to switch the brewer on, and press again to switch it off. The brewer also auto-offs 5 minutes after the last brew and restarts from this button.
moving_parts.axis: front to back (pressed into the face of the control panel)
moving_parts.pivot: no pin — returns on its own spring/membrane

moving_parts.how: Momentary illuminated button on the front control panel; pressed in to select an 8 oz cup size. Held together with the 12 oz button for 3 seconds (brewer plugged in but off) it enters Descale Mode; held with the brew button it toggles High Altitude Brewing Mode.
moving_parts.axis: front to back (pressed into the face of the control panel)
moving_parts.pivot: no pin — spring/membrane return

moving_parts.how: Momentary illuminated button on the front control panel; pressed in to select a 10 oz cup size.
moving_parts.axis: front to back (pressed into the face of the control panel)
moving_parts.pivot: no pin — spring/membrane return

moving_parts.how: Momentary illuminated button on the front control panel; pressed in to select a 12 oz cup size, and used with the 8 oz button to enter Descale Mode.
moving_parts.axis: front to back (pressed into the face of the control panel)
moving_parts.pivot: no pin — spring/membrane return

moving_parts.how: Large momentary illuminated button on the front control panel; pressed in to start the brew (and to start each descale/rinse cycle). It pulses when the brewer is ready and stays lit while brewing.
moving_parts.axis: front to back (pressed into the face of the control panel)
moving_parts.pivot: no pin — spring/membrane return

keurig k slim single serve pod coffee ma.source: Keurig K-Slim Use & Care Guide / Quick Start (manualslib copies: https://www.manualslib.com/manual/2398150/Keurig-K-Slim.html , https://www.manualslib.com/manual/2261260/Keurig-K-Slim.html , https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3490697/Keurig-K-Slim-K900.html , https://www.manualslib.com/guide/2924318/keurig-k-slim-single-serve-coffee-maker-manual.html) — labelled parts A Handle, B/C K-Cup Pod Holder Assembly, C Funnel, D K-Cup Pod Assembly Housing, E Drip Tray Plate, F Drip Tray, G Drip Tray Base, H Water Reservoir Lid, I Water Reservoir; Keurig support descaling page https://www.keurig.com/hub/support/how-to-descale-your-keurig-coffee-maker (8oz+12oz hold, brew button); Walmart listing https://www.walmart.com/ip/990248036 (46 oz removable reservoir, 8/10/12 oz sizes, removable drip tray for 7.0 in travel mugs); pod-holder removal procedure for the Keurig Slim: https://hollicoffee.com/how-to-remove-keurig-pod-holder/
keurig k slim single serve pod coffee ma.notes: The K-Slim has no doors, knobs, dials, wheels or separate latches — the handle is the only latch mechanism, and it both opens the brew head and closes/pierces the pod. Angles and travels are estimates from photos and geometry, not printed specs: the handle's useful swing is roughly 50–60° from closed to its rear stop; button travel on the flat front panel is about 1 mm (the panel is a low-travel backlit membrane-style set, so treat 1 mm as an upper bound); the drip tray slides roughly 60–80 mm forward before it clears its rails. The water reservoir lid on the K-Slim is a lift-off cap, not a hinged flap. The pod holder and funnel are cleaning-only removals (classed as detach), as is the drip tray plate; the drip tray itself is classed as a slide because the manual explicitly says to slide it toward you to remove it. The exit needle (in the pod holder base) and entrance needle (in the brew-head lid) move only as part of their carriers — the user does not actuate them directly, though the manual has the user poke them with a paperclip to clear them. The K-Slim + ICED variant shares this architecture but adds an ICED button to the control panel; the plain K-Slim does not have one.

keurig k mini single serve pod coffee ma.product_name: Keurig K-Mini single-serve K-Cup pod coffee maker (K-Mini, model K15-series successor; base model without the Plus/Go removable reservoir)

moving_parts.how: Grip the front lip of the handle and swing it up and back; the handle is the lever that lifts the top of the K-Cup pod assembly housing, opening the brew head and exposing the K-Cup pod holder, the funnel rim and the entrance needle underneath the lid. Lowering it closes and clamps the housing and drives the entrance needle through the pod foil. Manual: 'Lift the handle and place a K-Cup pod in the K-Cup pod holder. Lower the handle completely to close the lid.' Note: when the handle is up the reservoir drains into the brewer, so it must be down before filling.
moving_parts.axis: across the width (left-right horizontal axis), rotating in the front-to-back vertical plane
moving_parts.pivot: hinge pin at the rear top of the K-Cup pod assembly housing, behind the pod opening

moving_parts.how: Flat lid over the fill opening on the top rear of the brewer; the user lifts the front edge of the lid and it swings up and rearward, revealing the reservoir mouth with the MIN and MAX fill lines. Lowered back down flat to close before brewing. Manual: 'Lift the water reservoir lid and pour the water into the reservoir... Lower the lid.' The underside of the lid is wiped for cleaning.
moving_parts.axis: across the width (left-right horizontal axis), opening toward the rear
moving_parts.pivot: rear edge of the reservoir opening, at the top rear of the body

moving_parts.how: The tray sits on the drip tray base (M) on horizontal guides; the user pulls it straight toward themselves, keeping it level, until it comes free of the base. Manual: 'To remove, slide it toward you, keeping it level to avoid spilling.' Removing it reveals the drip tray base and gives clearance for a travel mug up to 7 in (178 mm) tall; it also empties the overflow reservoir (holds up to ~8-10 oz).
moving_parts.axis: front to back (pulled forward out of the base)
moving_parts.pivot: no pivot - horizontal rails/ledges in the drip tray base; disengages fully at the end of travel

moving_parts.how: The slotted plate the mug stands on simply lifts straight up and out of the drip tray for rinsing; dropped back in to locate on the tray rim.
moving_parts.pivot: comes off the top of the drip tray - no hinge, it just rests in the tray

moving_parts.how: With the handle lifted, grasp the top of the pod holder with one hand and push up on its underside from beneath the brewer with the other until it releases, then lift it out upward through the pod opening. To refit, align it with the opening using the two front ribs as a guide and snap it back in from the top. Removing it exposes the exit needle in the bottom of the housing.
moving_parts.axis: vertical (pushed/pulled up out of the housing)
moving_parts.pivot: snap-fit in the pod opening of the K-Cup pod assembly housing

moving_parts.how: The conical funnel ring sits on top of the removed pod holder; it is pulled straight off until it pops free of its friction/snap fit, and snapped back on the same way for refitting (done with the pod holder assembly out of the brewer).
moving_parts.axis: vertical, along the pod holder's own axis
moving_parts.pivot: snap/interference fit on the upper rim of the K-Cup pod holder

moving_parts.how: Round momentary push button on the top front of the brewer (illuminated, acts as the LED brew indicator); pressed straight down to start heating/brewing and it springs back. Lights solid/pulsing red or blue to show state.
moving_parts.axis: through the button's face (vertical, down into the top panel)
moving_parts.pivot: flat, spring-return membrane/dome switch under the button face

moving_parts.how: Small momentary push button on the brewer housing used to switch the brewer on and off; pressed straight in and springs back. It does not illuminate - the add-water/brew indicator flashing blue tells you it is on.
moving_parts.axis: through the button's face, perpendicular to the panel it sits in
moving_parts.pivot: flat, spring-return switch behind the button face

moving_parts.how: The cord is flexible and is tucked/wrapped into the cord-storage recess in the back/underside of the brewer for travel and storage, and pulled back out for use. No rigid joint - it bends only.
moving_parts.pivot: exit grommet at the rear of the brewer body

keurig k mini single serve pod coffee ma.source: Keurig K-Mini Use & Care Guide (official PDF): https://dam.keurig.com/content/dam/public-assets/support/kcom/pdf/KMini_UCG.pdf ; Keurig K-Mini UCG mirror: https://www.keurig.com/medias/1984-KMINI-UCG.pdf ; ManualsLib Keurig K-MINI Use & Care Manual (parts list A-M, cleaning steps): https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3956399/Keurig-K-Mini.html and https://www.manualslib.com/guide/4427745/keurig-k-mini-brewer-use-and-care-guide.html ; cleaning/removal Q&A: https://www.manualslib.com/answers/4444829/how-to-clean-keurig-k-mini-coffee-maker.html ; K-Mini Go UCG for contrast on the removable reservoir: https://dam.keurig.com/content/dam/public-assets/kcom_support/K-Mini_Go_Use_and_Care_Guide.pdf
keurig k mini single serve pod coffee ma.notes: Manual part labels: A Handle, B K-Cup pod holder, C Funnel, D K-Cup pod assembly housing, E Drip tray plate, F Drip tray, G Water reservoir lid, H Water reservoir, I Brew button, J LED indicator, K Power button, L Power cord, M Drip tray base. Important for the 3D model: on the base K-Mini the water reservoir (H) is NOT removable - it is integral to the body and is cleaned in place by wiping; only the K-Mini Plus and K-Mini Go have a reservoir that lifts straight up out of the base (and on the Go the lid lifts off rather than hinging). The base K-Mini also has no STRONG button (that is the K-Mini Plus/Go). Degree and millimetre figures are engineering estimates from photos and the illustrated manual steps, not published specifications: handle swing is roughly 45-60 degrees, the reservoir lid opens roughly 90-100 degrees to clear the fill mouth, drip tray slide-off travel is roughly 50-70 mm, button travel roughly 1-2 mm. The exact placement of the power button (rear face vs. side of the housing) varies with production run, and on some units the water reservoir lid can be lifted clear off its hinge posts for washing; treat those two as the least certain items. Non-user-moved internals (entrance needle above the pod, exit needle in the bottom of the holder, internal pump/valve) are excluded, as are consumables (the K-Cup pod and the mug).

audi e tron gt concept sports sedan.product_name: Audi e-tron GT concept (four-door electric gran turismo show car, 2018 Los Angeles Auto Show; basis of the production Audi e-tron GT quattro / RS e-tron GT)

moving_parts.how: Conventional front-hinged door; two hinges on the A-pillar at the leading edge of the door. Swings outward and forward to reveal the front seat and sill over the battery pack. Frameless side glass, so the glass drops slightly when the handle is operated.
moving_parts.axis: vertical (up-down axis at the front edge of the door)
moving_parts.pivot: A-pillar, front vertical edge of the door

moving_parts.how: Mirror image of the driver's door: hinges on the right A-pillar, opens outward and forward, frameless glass, reveals the front passenger seat.
moving_parts.pivot: A-pillar, front vertical edge of the door

moving_parts.how: Front-hinged rear door on the B-pillar; swings outward and forward, cut up into the roof shoulder, reveals the left rear seat of the 2+2 cabin.
moving_parts.pivot: B-pillar, front vertical edge of the rear door

moving_parts.how: Mirror image of the rear left door; B-pillar hinges, opens outward and forward to the right rear seat.
moving_parts.pivot: B-pillar, front vertical edge of the rear door

moving_parts.part: Exterior door handle (one per door, 4 total)
moving_parts.how: Slim grab handle set into the door skin; the outer end is pulled away from the body about the inboard end to release the latch, then springs back. On the show car the handles sit nearly flush with the body surface.
moving_parts.axis: vertical (handle tips outward about its inboard end)
moving_parts.pivot: inboard (front) end of the handle, inside the door skin

moving_parts.part: Front lid / bonnet over the front luggage compartment (approx. 100 l)
moving_parts.how: Clamshell front lid released from inside the cabin; hinges at its rear edge next to the windscreen base and lifts from the front, revealing the front luggage compartment above the front motor.
moving_parts.axis: across the car's width (left-right axis at the rear edge of the lid)
moving_parts.pivot: rear edge of the bonnet, at the base of the windscreen

moving_parts.part: Rear lid / boot lid (approx. 450 l rear compartment)
moving_parts.how: Separate boot lid (not a full hatch) in the sloping sportback tail; gooseneck/four-bar hinges at the front edge of the lid below the rear screen, lid swings up and rearward to reveal the rear luggage compartment.
moving_parts.axis: across the car's width (left-right axis at the front edge of the lid)
moving_parts.pivot: front edge of the boot lid, below the rear window

moving_parts.part: Charging flap, left front wing (plug-in charging socket)
moving_parts.how: Body-coloured flap in the left front wing, where a fuel flap would be; press or trigger it and it swings open (rearward/outward) to reveal the charging socket. Audi states the car is charged through this flap in the left front wing, or contactlessly by Audi Wireless Charging.
moving_parts.axis: vertical (flap swings about its forward vertical edge)
moving_parts.pivot: forward vertical edge of the flap, in the wing panel

moving_parts.part: Charging flap, right front wing (second socket)
moving_parts.how: Matching flap in the right front wing opening outward to a second charging socket. Confirmed on the production e-tron GT (AC left / DC right); on the concept only the left flap is described in the press material, so treat the right flap as optional on the 3D model.
moving_parts.pivot: forward vertical edge of the flap, in the wing panel

moving_parts.part: Side window glass (frameless, one per door)
moving_parts.how: Frameless glass runs in channels inside the door and drops straight down into the door cavity; it also drops a few millimetres automatically when the door is opened and seals up again when it is shut.
moving_parts.axis: vertical (glass travels up and down inside the door)
moving_parts.pivot: window track inside the door shell

moving_parts.how: Aerodynamic mirror on a slim stalk; the housing folds rearward against the body about the stalk base for parking, and the glass itself tilts within the housing for adjustment.
moving_parts.axis: vertical at the stalk base (housing folds rearward)
moving_parts.pivot: mirror stalk base on the door shoulder

moving_parts.how: Active spoiler hidden in the boot lid that rises out of the body at speed; on the production car it extends to two positions depending on driving situation, rising up and tilting rearward, then retracting flush.
moving_parts.axis: vertical with a rearward tilt (front to back)
moving_parts.pivot: linkage under the boot lid skin at the trailing edge

moving_parts.how: Two controllable inlets in the front apron feed the front brakes and the thermal-management radiators; louvre flaps rotate from closed (flush, low drag) to open when cooling is needed.
moving_parts.axis: across the car's width (louvres rotate on left-right axes)
moving_parts.pivot: louvre spindles inside the front apron ducts

moving_parts.how: Each wheel rotates freely on its hub about the axle centreline; the aero blades/covers on the rims turn with the wheel.
moving_parts.axis: across the car's width (left-right axle axis)
moving_parts.pivot: wheel hub centre

moving_parts.how: Both front wheels swivel about their steering axes when the steering wheel is turned, turning left and right inside the wheel arches.
moving_parts.axis: vertical (steering/kingpin axis at each front hub)
moving_parts.pivot: front suspension steering axis

moving_parts.how: Flat-bottomed multifunction wheel rotating about the inclined steering column; roughly 2.4 turns lock to lock, so about 430 degrees each way from centre. Column also adjusts for reach and height on the production car.
moving_parts.axis: along the steering column (front to back, inclined)
moving_parts.pivot: steering column centreline

moving_parts.how: Organ/hanging pedal pressed down by the right foot and spring-returned; travel is at the pad, rotating about the pedal pivot.
moving_parts.axis: front to back / vertical at the pad

moving_parts.how: Suspended pedal pushed forward and down about its pivot on the pedal box behind the bulkhead; spring returns it.

moving_parts.pivot: pedal box pivot behind the bulkhead, above the pad

moving_parts.how: Each front sport seat runs on a pair of rails bolted to the floor, sliding forward and back to set the driving position; the production seats add height and tilt adjustment (8- or 14-way).
moving_parts.pivot: seat rails on the cabin floor

moving_parts.how: Backrest reclines about the recliner mechanism at the base of the backrest where it meets the cushion; also tips forward to let people into the rear seats on a four-seat coupé layout.
moving_parts.axis: across the car's width (left-right axis at the seat hinge)
moving_parts.pivot: recliner hinge at the rear of the seat cushion, each side

moving_parts.how: Rear backrest folds forward about its lower edge to extend the boot through into the cabin. The concept is described as a fixed four-seater, so check the model before animating this.
moving_parts.pivot: lower edge of the rear backrest at the seat cushion

moving_parts.how: Visor swings down from the headlining about its spindle to shade the windscreen; it can also be unclipped at the inner end and swung sideways to the door window.
moving_parts.axis: across the car's width when swinging down; vertical when swung to the side window
moving_parts.pivot: visor spindle at the top of the windscreen header rail

moving_parts.how: Lid in the passenger side of the instrument panel, released by a catch and dropping forward/down about its bottom edge to reveal the stowage bin.
moving_parts.axis: across the car's width (left-right axis at the bottom edge)
moving_parts.pivot: bottom edge of the glovebox lid

moving_parts.how: Padded lid on the wide centre console between the seats, hinged at its rear edge and lifting up and back to reveal the stowage bin and interface sockets.
moving_parts.axis: across the car's width (left-right axis at the rear edge)
moving_parts.pivot: rear edge of the console lid

moving_parts.part: Drive selector (gear selector) on the centre console
moving_parts.how: Small toggle/rocker selector on the console: pushed forward or back for D and R and pressed for P, springing back to its rest position.
moving_parts.pivot: selector pivot inside the console housing

moving_parts.how: Flush buttons on the console/instrument panel that depress straight into their housings and spring back.
moving_parts.pivot: button guide in the panel

moving_parts.part: MMI touch display and virtual cockpit screens
moving_parts.how: Both screens are fixed black-panel glass surfaces with touch (and on the production car haptic) operation - the glass deflects a fraction of a millimetre, it does not tilt or retract. Model them as static panels.
moving_parts.pivot: screen mounting in the instrument panel / console

moving_parts.how: Mats (Econyl recycled material on the production car) unclip from retaining studs in the footwells and lift out for cleaning.
moving_parts.pivot: retaining clips in the footwell floor

moving_parts.how: Lift-out panel in the rear luggage compartment that is taken out to reach the underfloor stowage where the charging cables live; it lifts out of its recess.

moving_parts.how: The charging plug is pushed into the socket behind the wing flap and locked, then released and pulled straight out; the cable is stowed in the car. Not part of the body shell.
moving_parts.axis: along the socket axis (roughly across the car's width into the wing)
moving_parts.pivot: charging socket behind the wing flap

audi e tron gt concept sports sedan.source: Audi press release 'New leading role for electric performance: the Audi e-tron GT concept debuts in LA' (media.audiusa.com/releases/285) - four doors, four seats, 2.90 m wheelbase, charging via the flap in the left front wing or Audi Wireless Charging; paultan.org, 29 Nov 2018, 'Audi e-tron GT concept debuts at Los Angeles Auto Show' - two luggage compartments, 100 l front and 450 l rear; audi.com, 'The full appeal of electric driving: the Audi e-tron GT quattro' - two controllable cooling-air inlets, rear spoiler extending to two positions, 8-/14-way seats; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audi_e-tron (e-tron GT section, J1 platform shared with Porsche Taycan)
audi e tron gt concept sports sedan.notes: The e-tron GT concept is a specific, real show car (LA 2018), so it is treated as a known product, but it is a concept: Audi never published an owner's manual for it. Items confirmed for the concept itself by the press material are the four doors, the two luggage compartments (front and rear lids) and the left front-wing charging flap. The active cooling-air inlets, two-position rear spoiler, second (right-hand) charging flap, folding rear backrest and seat adjustment ranges are documented for the closely related production e-tron GT quattro / RS e-tron GT and are very likely represented on the concept body, so verify them on the actual 3D model before animating. All degree and millimetre figures are typical values for a car of this class (door swing, window drop, seat travel, pedal travel, 2.4 turns lock-to-lock steering) rather than published Audi figures - use them as sensible defaults, not specification. Purely cosmetic or static elements (Singleframe cover with its honeycomb-look surface, light units, aero blades fixed to the rims) have no user-operated motion except the wheel rotation already listed.

audi e tron gt electric sports sedan.product_name: Audi e-tron GT (J1 platform, 2021–present; incl. RS e-tron GT and 2025 facelift) — 4-door electric sports sedan

Its UV hood is the single most important articulation for a sim model: it is a lift-off box, NOT a hinged lid, so a hinge joint would be wrong - model it as a prismatic/removable part along +Z. Unlike the later Photon Mono, the Photon S has no lid sensor that pauses printing, so the cover is purely passive. Exact travel figures are not published in the manual: the ~250 mm cover lift, 60 mm vat lift, 20 mm USB insertion, 3 mm rocker throw and ~5 deg platform tilt are reasonable engineering estimates from the published external dimensions and photos, not quoted specs; the thumbscrew ranges are continuous threads so no single number applies. Items that are strictly maintenance disassembly (FEP frame, leveling cap screws) need the supplied Allen key. The Photon S is advertised with an upgraded internal air-filtration/ventilation system behind the rear vents, but I could not confirm from the manual whether its filter element is a user-removable cartridge, so I have left it out of the list rather than guess. I am also not fully certain whether the USB port on this revision sits on the front-right of the base beside the screen or on the rear panel near the power inlet - check the specific mesh before placing that joint.

cessna 182 skylane single engine light a.notes: The Cessna 182 Skylane is a real product line (Cessna/Textron Aviation, in production 1956–1986 and 1996–present). Details vary by variant: early 182s use a push-pull cowl flap knob, a between-seats flap lever or a non-preselect flap switch, and have no electric trim; 182S/T have a preselect flap switch, pedestal cowl-flap lever, electric pitch trim and (Nav III) G1000 knobs. Flap FULL is 40° on most 182s; some later Nav III aircraft are limited to 30°. Control-surface travel figures are nominal rigging values with roughly ±1–2° tolerance and differ slightly between serial-number ranges – check the model-specific service/maintenance manual before modelling exact stops. Ranges given for ailerons, elevator and rudder are total (sum of both directions). Landing gear is fixed (spring-steel mains, no retraction). Parts marked detach (cowl panels, filler caps, dipstick, gust lock, tow bar, covers, fire extinguisher) are removed for service, refuelling or ground handling rather than in flight.

cessna 310 twin engine light aircraft.notes: The 310 ran from 1954 to 1980 across many variants, so some items are model-specific: the nose baggage compartment and its side doors exist only on the long-nose 310R/T310R (1975-80); engine nacelle wing lockers are factory-fit from the 310I or retrofit; cowl flaps are manual-lever on early models and electric-switch on later ones; a left-hand crew door was an option on late aircraft. Flap travel is quoted as 45° on the earliest 310 in TCDS 3A10 and 35° on later models — I used 35 and flag the difference here. Degree and millimetre figures for cockpit controls (yoke travel, lever arcs, pedal travel, seat travel, door opening angles) are typical light-twin values given so they can be checked against a 3D model, not factory rigging dimensions; exact rigging figures come from the Cessna 310 Service Manual. The cabin door hinge side (forward edge, swinging forward) and the nose/locker door hinge lines (top edge, lifting up) should be verified against photographs of the specific variant being modelled. Flight controls, flaps, cowl flaps, gear and props are 'user moved' only indirectly, through the cockpit controls listed, but are included because they are the parts that visibly articulate on the airframe. Cowlings, fuel caps, dipsticks and cabin seats are the items that come off for servicing or cleaning and are marked detach.

nintendo switch pro game controller.notes: Only the controls listed above are user-moved. Travel figures for buttons (~1 mm) and stick tilt (~±22°) are typical measured/estimated values, not published Nintendo specifications, so treat them as approximate for rigging. Deliberately excluded: the USB Type-C port, NFC/amiibo touchpoint, charge LED, player LEDs and the IR/HD-rumble hardware are static features with no user motion. The Pro Controller has NO user-openable battery door, tray, lid or hatch - the 1300 mAh Li-ion pack is sealed inside behind tri-point (Y-type) screws and the two shell halves, so it is a service operation rather than a user-moved part. The grips are moulded into the shell and do not fold, detach or adjust, and there are no swappable stick caps, weights or back-paddle modules (unlike some third-party pads). The thumbstick caps are press-fit onto the shafts and can be pulled off during repair, but they are not designed as user-removable, so they are not listed as detach parts. ZL/ZR are digital switches despite their trigger shape, so in simulation their hinge is a short binary throw rather than a proportional axis.

Ranges: button travel and footpad deflection are approximate from the sealed-switch and sense-pad design (manual gives no figures); the Maghandle angle is approximate - riders report it releases only far enough (roughly 10-20 degrees, about 12 mm clear of the tire) to get fingers through before the magnet pulls it flush again, so it is a magnetically detented hinge rather than a fully folding handle. tesla model s sedan.source: Tesla Model S Owner's Manual (2021+), https://www.tesla.com/ownersmanual/models/en_us/Owners_Manual.pdf — sections on Doors, Opening and Closing (manual releases), Front/Rear Trunk, Charge Port, Touchscreen tilt, Glovebox, Seats, Mirrors, Windows, Wipers (Service Mode), Towing (tow eye), Cleaning/Maintenance (cabin filter, wiper blades); legacy Model S 2012–2020 owner's manual at https://www.tesla.com/ownersmanual/2012_2020_models/en_us/ (auto-presenting door handles, panoramic roof, manual HVAC vents); supporting coverage: notateslaapp.com article on the Model S/X display-tilt software update; electrek.co on the 2021 Model S/X refresh frunk and interior; teslamotorsclub.com threads on door handle/latch mechanisms.
tesla model s sedan.notes: Tesla Model S is a real, specific product, but it spans two very different interiors: the 2012–2020 car (portrait 17-inch fixed screen, auto-presenting motorised flush door handles, round wheel with two stalks, optional sliding panoramic roof, manually aimed HVAC vents) and the 2021+ 'refresh'/Plaid (landscape tilting screen, fixed press-to-pop paddle handles, yoke or round wheel, screen-only shift on early refresh cars with stalks returning from 2023, fixed glass roof, hidden vent). I have flagged which generation applies where it differs; a 3D model should be matched to one of them before the kinematics are applied. Angles and travels are engineering-plausible values checked against photos and the manual's descriptions — Tesla does not publish door-swing angles, window travel, screen-tilt degrees or pedal travel, so treat every number as approximate (±20%) and verify against the mesh. The tilt range of the 2021+ centre screen is left null because Tesla only names preset positions, not degrees. Nearly all 'latches' on this car are electric: doors, frunk, liftgate, charge port and glovebox all have no mechanical outside handle or button, so a simulation needs both the powered path and the cable backups (front-door lever, rear-door pocket cable, boot-trim charge-port cord, early-car hood cables behind the tow-eye cover). Excluded: suspension travel, HVAC flaps, headlight levelling and other parts the user never touches; a factory tow hitch was offered on some European Model S cars only, and the active rear spoiler belongs to the Model X, not the S.

tesla roadster sports car.notes: Identified as the first-generation Tesla Roadster (2008–2012), the Lotus Elise-based 2-seat targa EV — that is a specific real product with published manuals. (The 2017-announced second-generation Roadster is not in customer production and has no owner's manual, so it was not used.) Confirmed directly from the manual/quick reference: door opening via a touch pad in the door air inlet, trunk opened by a dash button on the lower left, by the key turned counter-clockwise in the external lock, or by a programmed fob button; trunk closed by pressing down on each side of the rear spoiler; T-shaped interior trunk escape handle at the rear of the trunk on the driver's side; charging port door and hood listed as separate openable items; and the bolt-off hard-top/soft-top removable roof using the supplied Torx tool (three header-rail trim bolts plus two rear bracket bolts). Items where the geometry is inferred rather than quoted and should be checked against the 3D model or photos before use: the exact hinge edge and swing angle of the trunk lid and of the front hood panel, the hinge edge and release mechanism of the charging port door, whether the fitted seats recline (Sport shell seats are fixed-back) and whether mirrors are power or manually adjusted (varies by 1.5/2.0/2.5 build). All angles and millimetre figures are typical-sports-car estimates unless stated in the manual; the manual does not publish opening angles. Wheel rotation, lug nuts, valve caps and wiper blades are included as user-moved service items; the hard-top, soft-top, wiper blades and toolkit are the parts that come fully off.
